payload.title:
Review and fix the attachment mime-types runtime bug from branch
fix/attachments-mime-default-import.

The existing candidate commit is:
59f8f2554

Do not trust the existing fix blindly.

Independently review it with Claude and Codex, run the relevant tests and
accounting safety gates, and if it is correct bring the task to
READY_TO_MERGE.

Do not merge or deploy automatically.

payload.reason: design phase failed: no JSON object found in agent output
adapter misreported an expired-OAuth 401 as a parse failure; envelope handling fixed
priorEscalations: design phase failed: no JSON object found in agent output

outOfScope: packages/server/tsconfig.json — enabling esModuleInterop changes the emit of every default import in the package; not a change to make while fixing one route
packages/server/package.json and nest-cli.json — build/test toolchain must stay fixed so the fix is proven against the emit that production actually uses
node_modules and .husky/_ — the candidate commit 59f8f2554 adds these as tracked symlinks (mode 120000) at repo root; they are contamination and MUST NOT land
packages/server/src/modules/Attachments/AttachmentsApplication.ts, S3UploadPipeline.ts, GetAttachment service and all other Attachments module files — the fault is in the import, not the service
The /:id/presigned-url route and its handler — it does not use mime
Every other default-import site in packages/server (knex, axios, zod, stripe, ioredis, js-money/lib/currency) — auditing them is allowed, changing them is not
Any accounting, ledger, journal, tax or reporting source file
Any merge to main and any deploy — explicitly forbidden by the task
invariants: I1 — GET /api/attachments/:id does not throw TypeError. Invoking the real AttachmentsController.getAttachment with a stubbed S3 output must complete without a TypeError from an undefined module binding.

I2 — The mime binding is a live object at runtime under the package's actual compiled emit (tsc via nest build, module=commonjs, allowSyntheticDefaultImports=true, esModuleInterop absent). Compile-time type-checking success is not evidence for this invariant.

I3 — Content-Disposition names the file <documentId>.<ext>, where ext is the mime-types extension for the S3 object's ContentType, and 'bin' whenever ContentType is absent or maps to no known extension.
I4 — Content-Type on the response equals the S3 object's ContentType, or 'application/octet-stream' when absent.
I5 — The response body is the exact bytes of the S3 object body, unmodified.
I6 — The final tree contains no tracked entry at node_modules or .husky/_ , and no tracked symlink (mode 120000) anywhere that was absent from the merge base.
I7 — Authorization is unchanged: getAttachment still requires AttachmentAction.View on AbilitySubject.Attachment, and every other Attachments route keeps the permission it had at merge base.
I8 — No file outside scopeAllowlist differs from the merge base in the final diff.
I9 — packages/server typecheck passes with zero new errors relative to merge base.
I10 — The accounting safety gates (Stage 0 suite and e2e baseline) produce the same result as on merge base; this change must be accounting-neutral.
I11 — The regression test fails if and only if the import is wrong. Restoring `import mime from 'mime-types'` with no other edit must turn the handler tests red.
falsifiablePredictions: P1 — Revert only the import line to `import mime from 'mime-types'`, keep the tests, run `pnpm --filter @bigcapital/server test -- Attachments.controller`. Prediction: all four getAttachment cases fail with 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading \'extension\')'. If they PASS, ts-jest is not reproducing the production emit and the entire diagnosis is unproven by the unit suite — escalate to P2 as the sole evidence.

P2 — Run `pnpm --filter @bigcapital/server build`, then inspect dist/modules/Attachments/Attachments.controller.js. Prediction with the fix: the emitted call is `mime.extension(` / `mime_types_1.extension(` with no `.default`. Prediction on the reverted import: the emit contains `.default.extension(`. If the fixed build still emits `.default`, the fix is wrong.

P3 — In the built dist, `node -e "const m=require('mime-types'); console.log(typeof m.extension, m.default)"`. Prediction: 'function' and undefined. If mime-types exposes a runtime `.default`, the stated root cause is false and the real 500 has another source — reject the fix and re-diagnose.

P4 — `git diff --name-status <merge-base>..HEAD`. Prediction: exactly the two Attachments files plus .ai/tasks/TASK-0007 metadata. Any node_modules, .husky/_ , tsconfig.json or 120000-mode entry falsifies I6/I8 and blocks READY_TO_MERGE.

P5 — Independent review by Claude and by Codex, run separately without sharing conclusions. Prediction: neither finds a defect in the handler body itself, and both locate the fault in the import. If the two reviewers disagree on root cause, the fix does not advance past REVIEW until adjudicated against P2/P3 evidence, which outranks both opinions.

P6 — Content type 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet' resolves to extension 'xlsx' against the real installed mime-types. If the test mocks mime-types instead of using the real module, the test cannot detect the bug it claims to guard and must be rejected.

P7 — `pnpm --filter @bigcapital/server test:stage0` and the e2e baseline produce identical pass/fail sets before and after the change. Any delta falsifies I10 and means this change is not accounting-neutral.
implementationConstraints: C1 — The candidate commit 59f8f2554 is NOT on ai/task-0007; HEAD still contains the broken `import mime from 'mime-types'`. Port the source and spec changes onto ai/task-0007 by cherry-pick or re-application, then drop the node_modules and .husky/_ symlink entries before the commit is proposed for merge.
C2 — The production change is confined to the import statement. Do not restructure getAttachment, do not add try/catch, do not alter header or buffer handling.
C3 — Use a namespace import (`import * as mime from 'mime-types'`) or a named import of the used function. Do not add esModuleInterop, do not add a require(), do not add a ts-ignore.
C4 — Do not touch packages/server/tsconfig.json even if it is the deeper cause. A tsconfig change is a separate, higher-blast-radius task; record it as a follow-up instead.

C5 — Tests must exercise the real AttachmentsController.getAttachment against the real mime-types module. Mocking mime-types, or asserting on mime.extension() in isolation, is not acceptable evidence.
C6 — Keep the existing authorization describe block in Attachments.controller.spec.ts intact; the file is modified, not replaced.
C7 — Do not merge, do not push to main, do not deploy. Terminal state for this task is READY_TO_MERGE.
C8 — If any invariant cannot be shown to hold, stop at REVIEW with the failing evidence recorded in .ai/tasks/TASK-0007/events.jsonl rather than advancing the state.
requiredTests: packages/server/src/modules/Attachments/Attachments.controller.spec.ts — getAttachment with ContentType 'text/plain' asserts Content-Type 'text/plain', Content-Disposition 'filename="doc-key-1.txt"', and body bytes preserved
packages/server/src/modules/Attachments/Attachments.controller.spec.ts — getAttachment with absent ContentType asserts Content-Type 'application/octet-stream' and a '.bin' filename
packages/server/src/modules/Attachments/Attachments.controller.spec.ts — getAttachment with an unmappable content type asserts the content type is echoed and the filename falls back to '.bin'
packages/server/src/modules/Attachments/Attachments.controller.spec.ts — getAttachment with the xlsx content type asserts the '.xlsx' extension, proving the real mime-types module is in play
packages/server/src/modules/Attachments/Attachments.controller.spec.ts — the pre-existing PermissionGuard cases for all six Attachments routes still pass unchanged
Accounting safety gate: pnpm --filter @bigcapital/server test:e2e (baseline comparison, not a rewrite of the baseline)
requiredRuntimeAcceptance: R1 — Mutation proof: with the fix in place the four getAttachment tests pass; with only the import reverted they fail with the exact production error string. Both runs' output must be captured in the task events log.

R2 — Emit proof: `nest build` output for Attachments.controller.js is inspected and shown to call mime.extension without a `.default` member access. This is the only evidence that speaks directly to the production artifact.
R3 — Module-shape proof: `require('mime-types').default` is undefined and `require('mime-types').extension` is a function in the installed dependency tree.
R4 — Tree cleanliness proof: `git diff --name-status` and a check for mode-120000 entries against the merge base, both clean.
R5 — Two independent reviews recorded — one Claude, one Codex — each with an explicit verdict, run without visibility into the other's conclusion.
R6 — Stage 0 accounting gate and e2e baseline both green, with output recorded. Not optional despite the change being non-accounting: the task is risk=high.
R7 — Task reaches READY_TO_MERGE only after R1–R6; no merge and no deploy is performed.
knownUnverified: U1 — No live HTTP call against a running server with a real S3/MinIO backend is planned. The 500 is reproduced at the handler level with a stubbed GetObjectCommandOutput, not end-to-end. If the production 500 had a second, independent cause downstream of mime, this design will not detect it.

U2 — The S3 stub asserts the shape of GetObjectCommandOutput (Body.transformToByteArray, ContentType) from the handler's usage, not from a captured real AWS SDK response. A shape drift in @aws-sdk/client-s3 would go unnoticed.

U3 — The candidate commit's audit claim — that knex, axios, zod, stripe and ioredis 'work by luck' via a runtime .default, and that the js-money default imports are elided — is inherited from the commit message and is not re-verified here. Those files are out of scope, so latent instances of the same defect may remain in the package.

U4 — The underlying tsconfig defect (allowSyntheticDefaultImports without esModuleInterop) is deliberately left in place. Any future default import from a CommonJS module in this package will reintroduce this class of bug. No lint rule is being added to prevent it; this should be filed as a follow-up task.
U5 — Behaviour under a future switch to the SWC builder or to ESM output is not tested. Namespace imports are expected to remain correct, but this is reasoning, not evidence.

U6 — Whether ts-jest resolves packages/server/tsconfig.json and therefore reproduces the production emit is assumed from ts-jest defaults; it is only actually established if P1 fails as predicted. If P1 does not behave as predicted, the unit suite carries no evidential weight for I2 and R2 becomes the sole proof.

U7 — The webapp calls the presigned-url route, so no user-facing regression is expected either way; the real-world blast radius of the original bug is inferred from that fact rather than measured from access logs.

findings.claim: I11 requires an impossible “if and only if” property. The proposed mutation run proves only that the tests detect this specific import regression; it cannot prove that an incorrect import is the only reason the tests can fail.
findings.scenario: Keep the correct namespace import, but make the S3 stub omit Body.transformToByteArray or run with the real mime-types dependency unavailable. The four handler tests fail even though the import is correct, contradicting the “only if” half of I11. Because C8 requires every invariant to be shown, the task cannot validly reach READY_TO_MERGE under the stated design.
findings.violatedInvariant: I11 — The regression test fails if and only if the import is wrong.
findings.evidenceAvailable: The design supplies only the one-direction mutation experiment in P1/R1. No experiment can establish that these integration-style handler tests have no other failure cause. Replace I11 with the falsifiable one-way requirement that reverting only the import makes otherwise-passing tests fail with the expected undefined-binding error.

findings.claim: The accounting/e2e acceptance rules disagree about whether an unchanged pre-existing failure is acceptable: I10 and P7 require equality with merge base, while R6 requires both gates to be green.
findings.scenario: Suppose test:e2e has one database-environment failure on merge base and exactly the same failure after the attachment change. This satisfies I10 and P7 because the pass/fail sets are identical, but fails R6 because the baseline is not green. Conversely, treating baseline equivalence as sufficient would violate the explicit non-optional R6 requirement. The workflow therefore has no unambiguous READY_TO_MERGE decision for this concrete state.
findings.violatedInvariant: I10 — Stage 0 and e2e must produce the same result as merge base; also C8/R7, which prohibit advancement until all invariants and R1–R6 hold.
findings.evidenceAvailable: I10 and P7 explicitly specify baseline equivalence; R6 explicitly says both gates must be green. The design must choose one policy—preferably require green results on both revisions, or explicitly permit identical documented baseline failures—and use it consistently.

payload.reasoning: I11 is stated as a biconditional and one half of it is not a property of the system under test — it is a claim about the space of all possible causes of a red test. The mutation experiment in P1/R1 establishes only the 'if' direction (wrong import ⇒ red). The 'only if' direction (red ⇒ wrong import) is false on its face for an integration-style handler test: a broken S3 stub, a missing dependency, a Nest wiring error or a changed header assertion all produce red with a correct import. This violates my own design discipline — an invariant must be a property that can hold and be shown to hold — and it collides with C8, which forbids advancing the state while any invariant is unshown. As written, no evidence anyone could gather would discharge I11, so the design contains a gate that cannot be passed. The severity is correct in mechanism though narrow in consequence: the remedy is an edit to the design text, not additional implementation or a re-run of any experiment already specified. The finding's own proposed replacement is the right one, and it preserves the useful content of the 'only if' half — the demand that the red be attributable to the import rather than to a broken harness — by pinning the failure mode instead of quantifying over all causes.
payload.requiredFix: Replace I11 with a one-directional, evidence-bearing property: 'I11 — The regression tests are sensitive to the import binding. With the namespace import in place, all four getAttachment cases pass. With only the import line reverted to `import mime from \'mime-types\'` and no other edit, those same cases fail, and the failure is a TypeError reporting a read of a property on undefined at the mime call site — not a stub, wiring or assertion error. mime-types is not mocked in either run (per C5).' Attribution of the red is carried by the required error string plus the green run on the same harness, so no claim is made about the set of all possible failure causes. No change to P1, R1, C5 or the required test list is needed; P1's existing wording already predicts the exact error string and should be read as the discharge of the restated I11.
payload.requiredEvidence: Two captured runs of `pnpm --filter @bigcapital/server test -- Attachments.controller` on identical trees differing only in the import line, both appended to .ai/tasks/TASK-0007/events.jsonl: (a) fixed tree — 4/4 getAttachment cases pass alongside the untouched PermissionGuard cases; (b) reverted tree — the same 4 cases fail with a TypeError naming an undefined binding at the mime call, while the PermissionGuard cases still pass (this last point is what distinguishes an import-attributable red from a harness-wide red). Plus a grep of the spec file showing no jest.mock of 'mime-types'.

payload.reasoning: The contradiction is real and, contrary to the finding's framing, its premise is not hypothetical — it is the current state of this repository. packages/server/test/e2e-baseline.json contains recorded `failed` entries with classifications (ASSERTION, UNKNOWN, BOOTSTRAP), and packages/server/test/e2e-runner.mjs documents its contract at lines 14-18 as 'exit 0 = run completed reliably and matches the baseline (improvements allowed)', with compareToBaseline (line 414ff) flagging only passed→failed transitions, missing tests and classification drift. So test:e2e is a differential harness by construction: it has no notion of 'green' meaning zero failures, and on merge base it is not green in that sense. R6's demand that the e2e gate be 'green' is therefore unsatisfiable as written, while I10 and P7 demand exactly what the harness actually measures. This is not a stylistic inconsistency between two acceptance rules; one of them contradicts the tool it names. Runtime artifact evidence outranks the design text here, and it resolves the conflict in favour of I10/P7. Note the two gates are not symmetric and the fix must not flatten them: test:stage0 is a plain jest run over the stage0 specs and green there does mean fully passing; only test:e2e is baseline-differential.
payload.requiredFix: Restate R6 per-gate and drop the word 'green' for e2e: 'R6 — (a) `pnpm --filter @bigcapital/server test:stage0` passes with zero failures, output recorded. (b) `pnpm --filter @bigcapital/server test:e2e` exits 0 against the committed test/e2e-baseline.json — no regressions, no missing tests, no REVIEW_REQUIRED items; improvements are permitted and must be reported but not written into the baseline. The baseline file is not regenerated (--write-baseline is forbidden for this task; e2e-baseline.json is outside scopeAllowlist and any modification to it also violates I8). Pre-existing baseline failures that recur unchanged do not block advancement. Neither gate is optional despite the change being non-accounting: the task is risk=high.' Leave I10 and P7 as they stand — they already state the correct policy — and align I10's wording to 'exit 0 / no regressions vs the recorded baseline' so the three clauses name one identical criterion.
payload.requiredEvidence: Recorded in .ai/tasks/TASK-0007/events.jsonl: the exit code and comparison block from `test:e2e` on the task branch showing the '--- baseline comparison ---' section with empty regressions and reviewRequired lists; the full stage0 jest summary showing zero failures; and `git diff --name-status` proving packages/server/test/e2e-baseline.json is unmodified (which is also the I8 check, so no separate run is required). If the e2e run exits 1 or 2, C8 applies and the failing comparison output is recorded at REVIEW rather than advancing the state.
